title: Hunting for Ghost Particles
summary: Built a reproducible ML pipeline to classify particle interactions from detector waveform data collected by the Majorana Demonstrator experiment.

details.overview: A capstone project analyzing waveform signals from high-purity germanium detectors to identify characteristics of particle interactions, packaged as a Dockerized pipeline for full reproducibility.
details.problem: distinguish event types and estimate energy from raw detector waveforms.
details.methods: time- and frequency-domain feature extraction, classification and regression models (scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM), Docker-based reproducibility.
details.outcome: generated energy spectrum visualizations and applied trained models to an unseen prediction dataset.

title: Recipe Simplicity Analysis
summary: Analyzed Food.com recipe data to find which recipe types need fewer steps, then built a model to predict step count from recipe features.

details.overview: Explored over 80,000 recipes and 700,000+ user interactions to identify which recipe categories tend to be quickest to prepare, then framed step-count prediction as a regression problem.
details.problem: find recipe types that are simpler and faster to prepare, and predict a recipe's number of steps.
details.methods: data cleaning, hypothesis testing and permutation tests, missingness analysis, tuned Random Forest Regressor.
details.outcome: cut test RMSE from 5.52 to 3.93 by adding tags and ratings as features and tuning hyperparameters.

title: Hospital Stay Predictors
summary: Built an interactive, scrollytelling site exploring which preoperative and demographic factors most affect how long patients stay in the hospital.

details.overview: Using a Korean hospital dataset from VitalDB, this project surfaces the preoperative factors most linked to longer hospital stays and lets visitors filter patients and explore the effect of each variable.
details.problem: identify which preoperative and demographic features most influence hospital stay length.
details.methods: Random Tree Classifier for feature importance, D3.js and Chart.js scrollytelling visuals, an interactive filter tool.
details.outcome: highlighted preoperative albumin and operation type as top predictors, with an interactive tool for exploring other variables.

title: Bikewatching
summary: An immersive, interactive map visualization of bike traffic in the Boston area during different times of the day, with a time-of-day slider to filter trips.

details.overview: A live station map that layers bike-share trip data over a Mapbox base map, letting visitors scrub through the day to see how traffic patterns shift at each station.
details.problem: show how bike-share traffic flow changes throughout the day at a station level.
details.methods: Mapbox GL for the base map, D3 for overlaying station markers, a time-of-day slider, and a color-coded departures/arrivals legend.
details.outcome: an at-a-glance view of which stations accumulate or deplete bikes as the day progresses.

title: Personal Portfolio Website
summary: The personal portfolio site you're browsing right now, hand-built with a custom light/dark theme, retro pixel styling, and interactive project popups.

details.overview: A fully custom personal site with no frameworks, covering the homepage, project showcase, and embedded resume, styled around a distinct pixel/retro visual identity.
details.problem: needed a personal site to showcase projects, resume, and contact info with a distinct look.
details.methods: hand-written HTML/CSS/JS, CSS custom properties for light/dark theming, and an accessible modal system for project details.
details.outcome: a fully responsive, dependency-free site deployed on GitHub Pages.

title: Bright Rhythms in the Rays

visual.alt: Sunshine vs EDM and R&B Streams Chart

summary: Analyzed and visualized the relationship between monthly sunshine duration and seasonal music streaming trends across contrasting genres (EDM vs. R&B).

details.overview: A data visualization project combining multi-city US historical weather data with US Spotify Top 200 daily streaming datasets (2017–2021) to explore how seasonal sunshine patterns correlate with mood and genre popularity.
details.problem: assess whether seasonal sunshine variations correlate with listener preferences for energetic music (EDM) versus mellow genres (R&B).
details.methods: multi-source data aggregation, date parsing, z-score standardization for multi-scale time series, side-by-side comparative chart design (pandas, Matplotlib, Plotly).
details.outcome: identified a strong positive correlation between peak sunshine months and EDM streams, alongside an inverse trend for R&B popularity during high-sunshine summer periods.

title: ESP32 Smart Theremin & Gesture ML
summary: Built an end-to-end TinyML gesture recognition system on an ESP32 microcontroller using ultrasonic and optical sensor data to classify physical hand interactions in real time.

details.overview: An 8-phase embedded machine learning project utilizing an ESP32 development board paired with ultrasonic distance and photoresistor modules to collect labeled sensor time-series, benchmark classical ML and deep learning models, and deploy on-device TinyML inference.
details.problem: capture multi-sensor continuous motion data and accurately classify distinct physical hand gestures with low latency on resource-constrained hardware.
details.methods: Arduino/C++ firmware timing optimization, signal filtering, time-domain feature engineering, model benchmarking (classical vs. deep learning), TinyML on-device deployment, and interactive Plotly Dash visualization.
details.outcome: successfully classified 5 core musical gestures (hold, glide, wave, swipe, mute) with real-time feedback and edge inference.

title: Career Landscape in Data Science & ML
summary: Conducted an exploratory data analysis on 20,000+ global Kaggle survey responses to uncover industry hiring requirements, compensation drivers, and technical tooling trends.

details.overview: A comprehensive career analytics study using Kaggle's community survey dataset (171 countries/territories) to evaluate educational qualifications, compensation benchmarks, task distributions across job roles, and core data science workflows.
details.problem: assess how educational degrees, technical experience (coding vs. ML), and global market demand influence role responsibilities and earning potential.
details.methods: categorical survey data cleaning, multiple-response frequency aggregation, contingency table analysis, cross-regional filtering, and multivariate visualization using R (tidyverse, dplyr, ggplot2, tidyr).
details.outcome: identified master's degrees as dominant in analytics/business roles (~50%) and PhDs in research (58%); found coding experience positively correlates with salary while ML experience showed negligible standalone correlation; mapped Python (~40%), SQL (~20%), and R (~15%) as top languages alongside linear/logistic regression (25%) and tree ensembles (35%).

title: Predictive Modeling of Daily Snowfall
summary: Trained Random Forest and XGBoost regression models on 49 years of Sierra Nevada climate data to predict daily snowfall accumulation from temperature and humidity patterns[cite: 6].

details.overview: A data science study analyzing 11,444 winter-season daily records (1970–2019) from UC Berkeley's Central Sierra Snow Lab and NOAA weather stations to model non-linear precipitation dynamics for California water management[cite: 6].
details.problem: accurately estimate total daily snowfall depth (cm) in the Sierra Nevada during snow-prone months (October through May) using surface temperature and humidity features[cite: 6].
details.methods: multi-source dataset merging, seasonal filtering, zero-inflation analysis, EDA, Random Forest Regression, and XGBoost modeling (Python, pandas, scikit-learn, XGBoost, seaborn)[cite: 6].
details.outcome: XGBoost achieved an RMSE of 7.42 cm and an R² of 0.490, highlighting maximum temperature and relative humidity as primary predictors while identifying the challenges of extreme tail-event underprediction[cite: 6].
